page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.2xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and supports instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and AVX512_VNNI, alongside AES cryptography acceleration. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate average multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth capabilities. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and PassMark CPU score both fall within the average tier. Similarly, memory read and write bandwidth tests for large blocks, as well as Redis SET operations, demonstrate middle-tier performance. However, single-core execution is a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core performance, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is also limited, aligning with the baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6.2xlarge offers a balanced resource density for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without the premium cost of memory-optimized or compute-optimized hardware. Given its average multi-core capabilities and balanced memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads, including database operations, moderate Redis deployments, and multi-threaded application servers that do not rely heavily on high single-core speeds or local disk storage.
